The Space Telescope: A Study of NASA, Science, Technology, and Politics (Smith)

NASA’s and ESA’s shared visible/UV space telescope, in low Earth orbit since 1990 and serviced five times by Space Shuttle missions through 2009. Still in operation 35+ years later, with major instruments installed by spacewalking astronauts and a primary mirror flaw corrected in 1993 by COSTAR (later replaced by instruments with built-in corrective optics).
Largest infrared space telescope; L2 orbit
One of NASA's four Great Observatories
Infrared Great Observatory; 16 years of data

The telescope that changed how humanity sees the universe. Launched 1990 with a flawed mirror — corrected by Space Shuttle astronauts in 1993. Has since observed 1.4 million celestial objects. Operating 34+ years.
